instruction: I need you to rotate this video 180 degrees and save it as 'Apple_Commercial_Flipped.mp4' on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires rotating a video 180 degrees in VLC and saving it. Evaluator performs frame-level verification by extracting sample frames from both source and output videos, rotating the source frame 180 degrees, and comparing it pixel-by-pixel with the output frame using RMSE comparison. This ensures the specific 180-degree rotation was applied, not just any transformation.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly implements frame-level pixel comparison to verify 180° rotation
Getter extracts frame #100 from both source and output videos, rotates source frame 180° using ffmpeg transpose filters
Metric performs RMSE pixel comparison between rotated source frame and output frame (threshold ≤ 0.05)
Secondary verification uses perceptual hash comparison as fallback (threshold ≤ 0.02)
Dimension check correctly validates that 180° rotation preserves width/height (unlike 90°/270°)
Frame-level verification directly confirms the specific 180° rotation was applied, not just any transformation
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add explicit check for ImageMagick tools (convert, compare) availability before attempting frame comparison
Handle edge case where video has fewer than 100 frames - use percentage-based frame selection (e.g., middle frame)
Add more informative error messages when frame extraction fails to help debug issues
Consider adding a sanity check to verify source video is not already the same as output (detect copy without transformation)
